## Technical Research Scope Confirmation

**Research Topic:** Entire.io Cross-Agent Integration for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode
**Research Goals:** Understand Entire.io architecture, cross-CLI integration model, hook points per agent, and how to build automated context injection — informing PRD/Architecture/Epics updates for full traceability

**Technical Research Scope:**

- Architecture Analysis - Entire.io checkpoint/shadow-branch/session model, data storage format, agent CLI detection
- Implementation Approaches - Hook integration patterns per CLI, shared session state formats
- Technology Stack - Entire.io CLI (Go), shadow git branches, checkpoint JSONL, AI summaries, CLI hook/extension APIs
- Integration Patterns - Cross-agent session bridging, parallel work cross-referencing, conflict detection, context injection
- Performance Considerations - Checkpoint recording overhead, session indexing latency, agent startup impact

**Research Methodology:**

- Current web data with rigorous source verification
- Multi-source validation for critical technical claims
- Confidence level framework for uncertain information
- Comprehensive technical coverage with architecture-specific insights

**Scope Confirmed:** 2026-03-03

## Technology Stack Analysis

### Entire.io CLI — Core Platform

**Language:** Go (compiled binary, MIT licensed)
**Version:** 0.4.9 (as of 2026-03-03)
**GitHub:** [entireio/cli](https://github.com/entireio/cli) — 3,311 stars
**Origin:** Built by former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke; $60M seed round announced alongside first product (Checkpoints)
**Install:** Homebrew (`brew install entireio/tap/entire`) or Go (`go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest`)

Entire.io is a Git-native observability layer for AI agent sessions. It hooks into both the AI agent and Git itself to capture code generation provenance — prompts, responses, files touched, token usage, tool calls — without polluting your commit history.

**Supported Agents (as of v0.4.9):**

| Agent | Status | Hook Location | Hook Format |
|-------|--------|---------------|-------------|
| Claude Code | **GA** | `.claude/settings.json` | JSON shell commands |
| Gemini CLI | **Preview** | `.gemini/settings.json` | JSON shell commands |
| OpenCode | **Preview** | `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` | TypeScript plugin |
| Cursor IDE | **Preview** | `.cursor/hooks.json` | JSON shell commands |

_Source: [GitHub README](https://github.com/entireio/cli), [Official Docs](https://docs.entire.io/introduction)_

### Entire.io Architecture Internals

**Shadow Branches:** During active sessions, Entire creates temporary local branches named `entire/<hash>-<worktree-id>` using go-git plumbing APIs — no checkout, no stash, no visible side effects. Deduplication is automatic via Git's content-addressable storage. Shadow branches are never pushed remotely.

**Checkpoint Metadata Branch:** The orphan branch `entire/checkpoints/v1` stores permanent metadata in a sharded directory structure:
```
entire/checkpoints/v1
└── a3/b2c4d5e6f7/           # 6-byte random checkpoint ID (12 hex chars)
    ├── metadata.json         # summary, attribution, tokens
    ├── 0/
    │   ├── full.jsonl        # complete transcript
    │   ├── prompt.txt        # user prompts
    │   └── context.md
    └── 1/                    # additional sessions if needed
```

**Bidirectional Linking:** Git commit trailers (`Entire-Checkpoint: a3b2c4d5e6f7`) create traceable links between code commits and session metadata. The `Entire-Attribution` trailer quantifies agent vs. human contributions (e.g., "73% agent (146/200 lines)").

**JSONL Transcript Parsing:** Entire reads the same JSONL files that agents write to disk. The CLI parses transcripts to extract modified files (from `tool_use` blocks), user prompts, token usage, and summaries. No APIs involved — purely filesystem-based parsing.

**Strategies:**
- `manual-commit` (default): Checkpoints created only at Git commit time
- `auto-commit`: Checkpoints after every agent response (finer-grained save points)

**Auto-Summarization:** When enabled (`strategy_options.summarize.enabled`), generates AI summaries at commit time using Claude CLI. Non-blocking failures.

_Source: [How Entire Works Under the Hood](https://julien.danjou.info/blog/how-entire-works-under-the-hood/), [Core Concepts](https://docs.entire.io/core-concepts)_

### Entire.io Agent Hook Model

Seven lifecycle hooks cover the full session:

| Hook Event | Purpose | Trigger |
|------------|---------|---------|
| `SessionStart` | Track session boundary | Agent starts |
| `SessionEnd` | Track session boundary | Agent exits |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | Capture human edits baseline | Before agent processes prompt |
| `Stop` | Trigger checkpoint save | After agent finishes a turn |
| `PreToolUse` | Monitor subagent spawning | Before tool execution |
| `PostToolUse` | Monitor subagent completion | After tool execution |
| `PostToolUse[TodoWrite]` | Capture task state | After todo updates |

Each hook executes shell commands like `entire hooks claude-code stop`. The hook reads agent-specific JSONL from well-known paths (e.g., Claude Code's session logs).

_Source: [Under the Hood article](https://julien.danjou.info/blog/how-entire-works-under-the-hood/), [Commands Reference](https://docs.entire.io/cli/commands)_

### Technology Adoption Trends

**Agent-Agnostic Tooling:** Entire.io represents a growing trend of agent-agnostic developer tools. Rather than vendor lock-in to Anthropic/Google/OpenCode-specific solutions, Entire stores everything in Git — portable across agents.

**Hook Standardization:** All three CLIs now have hook/extension systems (Claude Code since late 2025, Gemini CLI hooks since v0.26.0 January 2026, OpenCode plugins since launch). The patterns are converging:
- Session lifecycle events
- Tool interception (before/after)
- Context compaction hooks
- Shell command execution model

**Community Ecosystem Growth:** Gemini CLI has 1M+ developers with an extension marketplace. OpenCode has Oh My OpenCode (44 hooks, 26+ tools). Claude Code has plugins and BMAD. This creates opportunities for cross-agent tooling.

**Known Limitations of Entire.io:**
- No retention policy for `entire/checkpoints/v1` (grows forever)
- Squash merges break bidirectional linking (trailers disappear)
- No PR linkage (branch names recorded but no PR number/URL)
- Full transcripts stored in pushable branches (privacy concern for public repos)
- Auto-summarization requires Claude CLI (not agent-agnostic for this feature)

_Source: [Under the Hood article](https://julien.danjou.info/blog/how-entire-works-under-the-hood/), [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues)_

## Integration Patterns Analysis

### Communication Protocols — Unified stdin/stdout JSON

All three CLIs use a conceptually similar hook communication pattern, but with important differences:

| Aspect | Claude Code | Gemini CLI | OpenCode |
|--------|-------------|------------|----------|
| **Transport** | stdin → stdout (JSON) | stdin → stdout (JSON) | Function call → return value |
| **Block signal** | Exit 2 OR `permissionDecision: "deny"` | Exit 2 OR `decision: "deny"` | `throw new Error()` |
| **Allow signal** | Exit 0 (empty stdout) | Exit 0 (empty stdout) | Return nothing |
| **Context injection** | `additionalContext` field in hookSpecificOutput | `systemMessage` or `additionalContext` | Modify args or return context |
| **Handler types** | Command, HTTP, Prompt, Agent | Command only | TypeScript/JavaScript function |
| **Timeout default** | 60s | 60s | N/A (sync JS execution) |
| **Async support** | Yes (background hooks with later injection) | No | Yes (async functions) |

**Key Insight for Entire.io:** The Entire.io CLI already implements adapter layers per agent. For Claude Code and Gemini CLI, it writes JSON shell command hooks into `settings.json`. For OpenCode, it generates a TypeScript plugin file at `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. This means the protocol translation is handled by Entire.io — consumers don't need to care about per-CLI differences.

_Source: [Claude Code Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [Gemini CLI Hooks Reference](https://geminicli.com/docs/hooks/reference/), [OpenCode Plugins Docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/)_

### Hook Event Mapping Across CLIs

Entire.io needs to map its 7 lifecycle events to each CLI's event model:

| Entire.io Hook | Claude Code Event | Gemini CLI Event | OpenCode Event |
|----------------|-------------------|------------------|----------------|
| `SessionStart` | `SessionStart` | `SessionStart` | `session.created` |
| `SessionEnd` | `SessionEnd` | `SessionEnd` | `session.idle` or `session.deleted` |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | `UserPromptSubmit` | `BeforeAgent` | `tui.command.execute` |
| `Stop` (checkpoint trigger) | `Stop` | `AfterAgent` | `session.updated` |
| `PreToolUse` (subagent) | `PreToolUse` (matcher: `Agent`) | `BeforeTool` | `tool.execute.before` |
| `PostToolUse` (subagent) | `PostToolUse` (matcher: `Agent`) | `AfterTool` | `tool.execute.after` |
| `PostToolUse[TodoWrite]` | `PostToolUse` (matcher: `TodoWrite`) | `AfterTool` (matcher: `todo`) | `todo.updated` |

### Context Injection Patterns — The Key Integration Point

The most valuable pattern for Cohezion's agent context awareness is **SessionStart context injection**. Each CLI supports injecting context when a session starts:

**Claude Code:**
```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "SessionStart",
    "additionalContext": "Context string injected into Claude's system prompt"
  }
}
```
The `additionalContext` is prepended to the first prompt. Non-JSON stdout from SessionStart hooks is also injected directly into context.

**Gemini CLI:**
```json
{
  "systemMessage": "Context injected as system message",
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "additionalContext": "Additional context appended to prompt"
  }
}
```
Both `systemMessage` and `additionalContext` are supported. The `source` field in input (`startup|resume|clear`) allows different injection behavior per trigger.

**OpenCode:**
```typescript
export const ContextPlugin = async ({ project }) => ({
  hooks: {
    "session.created": async (input) => {
      // Inject context via custom tool or tui.prompt.append
    },
    "experimental.session.compacting": async (input) => {
      // Inject context that survives compaction
    }
  }
})
```
OpenCode uses `experimental.session.compacting` for context that must survive compaction — critical for persistent session awareness.

_Source: [Claude Code Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [Gemini CLI Hooks Reference](https://geminicli.com/docs/hooks/reference/), [OpenCode Plugins](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/)_

### Entire.io Data Access Patterns

For context injection to work, a SessionStart hook needs to query Entire.io's data. Available CLI commands:

| Command | Output | Use Case |
|---------|--------|----------|
| `entire status` | Active sessions, agent types, token counts | "What's happening now across all agents?" |
| `entire explain --short` | Checkpoint list with session summaries | "What was accomplished in recent sessions?" |
| `entire explain --checkpoint <id> --short` | Single checkpoint summary | "What did session X do?" |
| `entire explain --session <id>` | All checkpoints for a session | "Full history of a specific session" |
| `entire explain --generate` | AI-generated summary (requires Claude CLI) | "Summarize what happened for injection" |

**Performance Characteristics:**
- `entire status`: ~200ms (reads local metadata)
- `entire explain --short`: ~500ms (reads checkpoint branch)
- `entire explain --generate`: 3-10s (calls Claude CLI for AI summary)
- `entire rewind --list`: ~300ms (reads shadow branches)

**Integration Pattern: SessionStart → entire status → format → inject as context**

A shell hook can be shared across Claude Code and Gemini CLI (both use shell commands). OpenCode requires a TypeScript wrapper that shells out to the `entire` binary.

_Source: [Entire CLI Commands](https://docs.entire.io/cli/commands), local testing on this project_

### Cross-Agent Session Visibility Architecture

The core architectural challenge: making each agent aware of what other agents are doing in parallel. The data flow:

```
Agent A (Claude Code) starts session
  └→ Entire hooks capture SessionStart
      └→ Shadow branch created
          └→ Checkpoints accumulate on turns

Agent B (Gemini CLI) starts session
  └→ SessionStart hook fires
      └→ Hook runs: entire status
          └→ Sees Agent A's active session
              └→ Injects: "Claude Code session active on branch X, working on Y"
```

**Conflict Detection Pattern:**
```
SessionStart hook:
  1. Run `entire status` → parse JSON output
  2. Filter for sessions on same branch or touching same files
  3. If overlap detected → inject warning context
  4. If no overlap → inject awareness context (FYI only)
```

**File-Level Conflict Detection (Advanced):**
```
Stop/AfterAgent hook:
  1. Run `entire explain --checkpoint <latest> --short`
  2. Extract files_touched list
  3. Compare against other active sessions' files_touched
  4. If overlap → inject merge-risk warning
```

_Source: Architecture derived from [Entire.io Core Concepts](https://docs.entire.io/core-concepts) and [Under the Hood](https://julien.danjou.info/blog/how-entire-works-under-the-hood/)_

### Security Patterns

**Secret Redaction:** Entire.io performs best-effort redaction of API keys, tokens, and credentials when writing to `entire/checkpoints/v1`. However:
- Shadow branches during active sessions may contain unredacted data
- Redaction is pattern-based, not comprehensive
- Public repos expose full session transcripts

**Hook Security:**
- Claude Code: Hooks run with user permissions, outside the Bash tool sandbox
- Gemini CLI: Project-level hooks fingerprinted; warns on changes from git pull
- OpenCode: Plugin hooks don't intercept subagent tool calls (known bug — [Issue #5894](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/5894))

**Recommendation for Cohezion:** Since Cohezion is a private repo with sensitive research data:
1. Use `.entire/settings.local.json` for any API keys in summarization config
2. Review `entire/checkpoints/v1` before pushing to remote
3. Consider `--skip-push-sessions` for sensitive branches

_Source: [GitHub README](https://github.com/entireio/cli), [Entire Configuration](https://docs.entire.io/cli/configuration)_

## Architectural Patterns and Design

### Recommended System Architecture: Observer-Mediated Hub-and-Spoke

After analyzing multi-agent coordination patterns, the architecture that best fits Cohezion's Entire.io integration is a **hub-and-spoke pattern with observer-mediated context sharing**, where Entire.io serves as the hub and each agent CLI is a spoke.

```
                    ┌──────────────────────┐
                    │   Entire.io Hub      │
                    │  (Git Shadow Branch)  │
                    │  entire/checkpoints   │
                    │  /v1 metadata         │
                    └──────┬───────────────┘
                           │
              ┌────────────┼────────────────┐
              │            │                │
    ┌─────────▼──┐  ┌─────▼──────┐  ┌──────▼─────┐
    │ Claude Code │  │ Gemini CLI │  │  OpenCode  │
    │   Hooks     │  │   Hooks    │  │  Plugin    │
    │ (JSON cmd)  │  │ (JSON cmd) │  │ (TS func)  │
    └─────────────┘  └────────────┘  └────────────┘
```

**Why this pattern over alternatives:**

| Pattern | Fit | Reason |
|---------|-----|--------|
| Hub-and-Spoke (Entire.io as hub) | **Best** | Entire.io already acts as centralized session store; agents don't need to talk directly to each other |
| Peer-to-Peer (agents talk directly) | Poor | No agent-to-agent protocol exists; CLIs don't know about each other |
| Blackboard (shared memory space) | Medium | Git shadow branches are a blackboard, but too slow for real-time coordination |
| Orchestrator-Worker | Poor | No single agent coordinates others; all agents are independent |

**Key architectural insight:** We don't need agents to communicate with each other in real-time. We need each agent to be **aware of what other agents have done and are doing** when it starts. This is a read-only context injection problem, not a bidirectional communication problem. Entire.io's existing `entire status` command provides the data; we just need hooks to inject it.

_Source: [Google's Multi-Agent Patterns (InfoQ)](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/01/multi-agent-design-patterns/), [Microsoft Multi-Agent Reference Architecture](https://microsoft.github.io/multi-agent-reference-architecture/docs/reference-architecture/Patterns.html), [Event-Driven Multi-Agent Systems (Confluent)](https://www.confluent.io/blog/event-driven-multi-agent-systems/)_

### Cross-Runtime Translation Pattern (Lessons from GSD)

The [GSD project](https://github.com/gsd-build/get-shit-done) (used at Amazon, Google, Shopify, Webflow) solved the exact same cross-runtime problem: one codebase targeting Claude Code, OpenCode, and Gemini CLI. Their architecture provides a proven pattern:

**Canonical Format + Install-Time Transformation:**
```
Canonical (Claude Code format)
    ↓
[Runtime Detector]
    ├→ Claude Code: Copy unchanged to ~/.claude/
    ├→ OpenCode: Flatten commands, map tools, convert frontmatter → ~/.config/opencode/
    └→ Gemini CLI: Convert MD→TOML, normalize tools, strip MCP → ~/.gemini/
```

**Key Transformations Required:**

| Aspect | Claude Code | Gemini CLI | OpenCode |
|--------|-------------|------------|----------|
| Hook format | JSON in `settings.json` | JSON in `settings.json` | TypeScript in `plugins/` |
| Tool names | PascalCase (`Read`, `Write`) | snake_case (`read_file`, `write_file`) | lowercase (`read`, `write`) |
| Command structure | Nested dirs | TOML files | Flat files |
| Config location | `~/.claude/` | `~/.gemini/` | `~/.config/opencode/` |

**Relevance to Cohezion:** Entire.io already implements per-agent adapters (JSON for Claude/Gemini, TypeScript for OpenCode). Our custom context injection hooks should follow the same pattern — write the logic once in a shell script, then wrap it for each runtime.

_Source: [GSD Architecture (DeepWiki)](https://deepwiki.com/gsd-build/get-shit-done), [One Codebase Three Runtimes (Rick Hightower)](https://medium.com/@richardhightower/one-codebase-three-runtimes-how-gsd-targets-claude-code-opencode-and-gemini-cli-29c98cfe96c6)_

### Context Injection Architecture

The core architectural component is a **SessionStart context injector** — a hook/plugin that runs when any agent starts a session and injects awareness of parallel sessions.

**Proposed Architecture:**

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ SessionStart Hook (shared shell script)              │
│                                                      │
│  1. entire status --quiet → parse active sessions    │
│  2. Filter: same branch? same files? conflicts?      │
│  3. Format: concise context string                   │
│  4. Return: JSON with additionalContext               │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                   │
     ┌─────────────┼─────────────────────┐
     │             │                     │
┌────▼────┐  ┌────▼────┐  ┌─────────────▼──────────┐
│ Claude  │  │ Gemini  │  │ OpenCode               │
│ Hook    │  │ Hook    │  │ Plugin                  │
│ wrapper │  │ wrapper │  │ wrapper                 │
│ (JSON)  │  │ (JSON)  │  │ (TS → shell out)       │
└─────────┘  └─────────┘  └────────────────────────┘
```

**Three-layer design:**

1. **Core Logic Layer** (`entire-context.sh`): A single shell script that queries `entire status`, formats context, and outputs JSON. Agent-agnostic — pure data transformation.

2. **Adapter Layer** (per-CLI wrappers):
   - Claude Code: Shell hook in `.claude/settings.json` that calls `entire-context.sh` and returns `{ hookSpecificOutput: { additionalContext: "..." } }`
   - Gemini CLI: Shell hook in `.gemini/settings.json` that calls `entire-context.sh` and returns `{ systemMessage: "..." }`
   - OpenCode: TypeScript plugin in `.opencode/plugins/entire-context.ts` that shells out to `entire-context.sh` and returns context via the plugin API

3. **Output Format Layer**: Each adapter formats the core logic output into the CLI-specific JSON/return format.

**Design Principles:**
- **DRY:** Core logic written once, adapters are thin wrappers
- **Fail-open:** If `entire status` fails, the hook returns empty context (no blocking)
- **Performance budget:** <500ms total (entire status ~200ms + formatting ~50ms + overhead ~250ms)
- **Non-blocking:** If hook exceeds timeout, agent starts without context (graceful degradation)

_Source: Architecture derived from [Claude Code Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [Gemini CLI Hooks](https://geminicli.com/docs/hooks/), [OpenCode Plugins](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/), and GSD translation pattern_

### Data Architecture: Entire.io's Git-Native Storage

Entire.io's storage architecture uses Git primitives exclusively — no external databases, no cloud services, no additional infrastructure:

```
Git Repository
├── main (your code, clean history)
├── entire/<hash>-<worktree-id> (temporary shadow branches, local only)
└── entire/checkpoints/v1 (permanent metadata, pushable)
    └── a3/b2c4d5e6f7/
        ├── metadata.json    # summary, attribution, tokens
        ├── 0/
        │   ├── full.jsonl   # complete transcript
        │   ├── prompt.txt   # user prompts
        │   └── context.md   # context snapshot
        └── 1/               # additional sessions
```

**Architectural Strengths:**
- Zero infrastructure cost (uses Git you already have)
- Collision-free multi-developer pushes (12-char random hex IDs)
- Tree union merges (no merge conflicts on `entire/checkpoints/v1`)
- Content-addressable deduplication (identical files share blobs)
- Transport for free (git push/pull handles distribution)

**Architectural Weaknesses:**
- No retention policy (metadata branch grows forever)
- Squash merges destroy commit trailers (breaks bidirectional links)
- No real-time session visibility (must query CLI for status)
- Transcript privacy concerns for public repos
- No query indexing (linear scan for searches)

_Source: [How Entire Works Under the Hood](https://julien.danjou.info/blog/how-entire-works-under-the-hood/), [Entire Core Concepts](https://docs.entire.io/core-concepts)_

### Scalability and Performance Considerations

| Concern | Current State | Mitigation |
|---------|---------------|------------|
| Shadow branch accumulation | `entire clean` for local cleanup | Schedule periodic cleanup via cron or git hook |
| Checkpoint metadata growth | No retention policy | Implement custom `entire/checkpoints/v1` pruning script |
| SessionStart hook latency | ~200-500ms for `entire status` | Cache status output for 30s; invalidate on git commit |
| Transcript size per session | Can exceed 1MB per session | Not a concern for context injection (we only read metadata, not transcripts) |
| Multiple concurrent sessions | 24 active sessions on this project | `entire status` handles this; output grows linearly with sessions |
| Git checkout heaviness | Thousands of turns accumulate data | `entire/checkpoints/v1` is metadata-only (JSON, not code) |

**Performance Budget for Context Injection:**
```
SessionStart hook total budget: 1000ms (well within 60s timeout)
  ├── entire status:     ~200ms
  ├── JSON parsing:      ~50ms
  ├── Formatting:        ~50ms
  ├── Adapter overhead:  ~100ms
  └── Margin:            ~600ms
```

_Source: Local performance measurements, [Entire Configuration](https://docs.entire.io/cli/configuration)_

### Security Architecture

**Threat Model for Cross-Agent Context Injection:**

| Threat | Risk | Mitigation |
|--------|------|------------|
| Sensitive data in injected context | Medium | Context injection uses `entire status` (session metadata only, not transcripts) |
| Hook tampering via git pull | Medium | Gemini CLI fingerprints project hooks; warns on changes. Claude Code requires explicit approval. OpenCode uses trusted plugin dirs. |
| Secret leakage in checkpoints | High for public repos | Entire performs best-effort redaction; recommend `--skip-push-sessions` for sensitive branches |
| Subagent bypass of hooks | Known bug (OpenCode) | OpenCode `tool.execute.before` doesn't intercept subagent calls ([Issue #5894](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/5894)) |
| Stale session data injection | Low | Status is live (not cached); stale data is misleading but not harmful |

**Recommended Security Posture:**
1. Context injection hooks should ONLY query `entire status` (metadata) — never raw transcripts
2. Use `.entire/settings.local.json` for any API keys (gitignored)
3. Review `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch before pushing to public remotes
4. For Cohezion (private repo): moderate risk; standard precautions sufficient

_Source: [Entire Configuration](https://docs.entire.io/cli/configuration), [GitHub README Security Section](https://github.com/entireio/cli)_

### Traceability Architecture — PRD to Checkpoint Chain

The complete traceability chain connecting BMAD planning artifacts to Entire.io session data:

```
BMAD PRD (FR-X.Y)
  └→ Architecture (ADR-N)
      └→ Epic (Epic 12: Sovereign-Sync)
          └→ Story (Story 12.X)
              └→ Sprint Task
                  └→ Git Branch (session-N-feature)
                      └→ Git Commit
                          ├→ Entire-Checkpoint: <12-hex-id>
                          │   └→ Session Transcript (prompts, decisions, token cost)
                          └→ Entire-Attribution: X% agent (N/M lines)
```

**Query Paths:**
- **Forward (Plan → Code):** PRD → Epic → Story → Branch → Commits → Checkpoints
- **Reverse (Code → Plan):** `entire explain --commit <sha>` → Session → Prompts → Intent → Story → Epic

**Squash Merge Workaround:** Since `cz worktree sync` uses squash merge (destroying trailers), the workaround is:
1. Before squash: record checkpoint IDs from the feature branch commits
2. Add checkpoint references to the squash commit message body (not trailers)
3. Or: store checkpoint → story mapping in Entire's metadata.json

_Source: [Core Concepts](https://docs.entire.io/core-concepts), [Under the Hood](https://julien.danjou.info/blog/how-entire-works-under-the-hood/), architecture analysis for Cohezion's existing `cz worktree` workflow_

### Deployment Architecture

**No additional infrastructure required.** The entire integration is local developer tooling:

```
Developer Machine
├── Entire.io CLI (Go binary, already installed)
├── Claude Code (with hooks in .claude/settings.json)
├── Gemini CLI (needs hooks in .gemini/settings.json)
├── OpenCode (needs plugin in .opencode/plugins/)
└── Custom Hooks
    ├── .claude/hooks/entire-context.sh    (core logic)
    ├── .gemini/hooks/entire-context.sh    (symlink or copy)
    └── .opencode/plugins/entire-context.ts (TS wrapper)
```

**CI/CD Impact:** Zero. Entire.io is local dev tooling. No build changes, no new dependencies in production. The `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch can optionally be pushed for team visibility.

**Team Onboarding:** `entire enable --agent claude-code --agent gemini --agent opencode` + copy hook files. Could be automated via a setup script or Makefile target.

_Source: [Entire CLI README](https://github.com/entireio/cli), [Entire Quickstart](https://docs.entire.io/quickstart)_

## Technology Stack Analysis

### Entire.io CLI — Core Platform

**Language:** Go (compiled binary, MIT licensed)
**Version:** 0.4.9 (as of 2026-03-03)
**GitHub:** [entireio/cli](https://github.com/entireio/cli) — 3,311 stars
**Origin:** Built by former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke; $60M seed round announced alongside first product (Checkpoints)
**Install:** Homebrew (`brew install entireio/tap/entire`) or Go (`go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest`)

Entire.io is a Git-native observability layer for AI agent sessions. It hooks into both the AI agent and Git itself to capture code generation provenance — prompts, responses, files touched, token usage, tool calls — without polluting your commit history.

**Supported Agents (as of v0.4.9):**

| Agent | Status | Hook Location | Hook Format |
|-------|--------|---------------|-------------|
| Claude Code | **GA** | `.claude/settings.json` | JSON shell commands |
| Gemini CLI | **Preview** | `.gemini/settings.json` | JSON shell commands |
| OpenCode | **Preview** | `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` | TypeScript plugin |
| Cursor IDE | **Preview** | `.cursor/hooks.json` | JSON shell commands |

_Source: [GitHub README](https://github.com/entireio/cli), [Official Docs](https://docs.entire.io/introduction)_

### Entire.io Architecture Internals

**Shadow Branches:** During active sessions, Entire creates temporary local branches named `entire/<hash>-<worktree-id>` using go-git plumbing APIs — no checkout, no stash, no visible side effects. Deduplication is automatic via Git's content-addressable storage. Shadow branches are never pushed remotely.

**Checkpoint Metadata Branch:** The orphan branch `entire/checkpoints/v1` stores permanent metadata in a sharded directory structure:
```
entire/checkpoints/v1
└── a3/b2c4d5e6f7/           # 6-byte random checkpoint ID (12 hex chars)
    ├── metadata.json         # summary, attribution, tokens
    ├── 0/
    │   ├── full.jsonl        # complete transcript
    │   ├── prompt.txt        # user prompts
    │   └── context.md
    └── 1/                    # additional sessions if needed
```

**Bidirectional Linking:** Git commit trailers (`Entire-Checkpoint: a3b2c4d5e6f7`) create traceable links between code commits and session metadata. The `Entire-Attribution` trailer quantifies agent vs. human contributions (e.g., "73% agent (146/200 lines)").

**JSONL Transcript Parsing:** Entire reads the same JSONL files that agents write to disk. The CLI parses transcripts to extract modified files (from `tool_use` blocks), user prompts, token usage, and summaries. No APIs involved — purely filesystem-based parsing.

**Strategies:**
- `manual-commit` (default): Checkpoints created only at Git commit time
- `auto-commit`: Checkpoints after every agent response (finer-grained save points)

**Auto-Summarization:** When enabled (`strategy_options.summarize.enabled`), generates AI summaries at commit time using Claude CLI. Non-blocking failures.

_Source: [How Entire Works Under the Hood](https://julien.danjou.info/blog/how-entire-works-under-the-hood/), [Core Concepts](https://docs.entire.io/core-concepts)_

### Entire.io Agent Hook Model

Seven lifecycle hooks cover the full session:

| Hook Event | Purpose | Trigger |
|------------|---------|---------|
| `SessionStart` | Track session boundary | Agent starts |
| `SessionEnd` | Track session boundary | Agent exits |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | Capture human edits baseline | Before agent processes prompt |
| `Stop` | Trigger checkpoint save | After agent finishes a turn |
| `PreToolUse` | Monitor subagent spawning | Before tool execution |
| `PostToolUse` | Monitor subagent completion | After tool execution |
| `PostToolUse[TodoWrite]` | Capture task state | After todo updates |

Each hook executes shell commands like `entire hooks claude-code stop`. The hook reads agent-specific JSONL from well-known paths (e.g., Claude Code's session logs).

_Source: [Under the Hood article](https://julien.danjou.info/blog/how-entire-works-under-the-hood/), [Commands Reference](https://docs.entire.io/cli/commands)_

### Claude Code Hook System

**12 lifecycle events, 3 handler types (command, prompt, agent)**

| Event | Timing | Can Block? |
|-------|--------|------------|
| `SessionStart` | Session begins | No |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | User submits prompt | No |
| `PreToolUse` | Before tool execution | **Yes** |
| `PostToolUse` | After tool success | No |
| `PostToolUseFailure` | After tool failure | No |
| `Notification` | Permission/notification | No |
| `Stop` | Agent finishes responding | No |
| `SubagentStop` | Subagent finishes | No |
| `PreCompact` | Before context compaction | No |

**Configuration:** JSON in `.claude/settings.json` at three levels: `~/.claude/settings.json` (global), `.claude/settings.json` (project), `.claude/settings.local.json` (personal).

**Handler Types:**
- **Command:** Shell commands (deterministic)
- **Prompt:** LLM evaluation (semantic)
- **Agent:** Deep analysis with tool access

**Current Entire.io Integration Status (this project):** **FULLY INSTALLED** — SessionStart (1), SessionEnd (1), UserPromptSubmit (1), Stop (1), PreToolUse (2), PostToolUse (2) hooks active.

_Source: [Claude Code Hooks Guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks-guide), [aiorg.dev Complete Guide](https://aiorg.dev/blog/claude-code-hooks)_

### Gemini CLI Hook System

**11 lifecycle events, command-based handlers only**

| Event | Timing | Can Block? |
|-------|--------|------------|
| `SessionStart` | Session begins | No |
| `SessionEnd` | Session ends | No |
| `BeforeAgent` | After prompt, before planning | **Yes** |
| `AfterAgent` | Agent loop completes | **Yes** (retry/halt) |
| `BeforeModel` | Before LLM request | **Yes** (modify/mock) |
| `AfterModel` | After LLM response | **Yes** (filter/redact) |
| `BeforeToolSelection` | Before tool selection | **Yes** (filter tools) |
| `BeforeTool` | Before tool execution | **Yes** (validate/block) |
| `AfterTool` | After tool execution | No |
| `PreCompress` | Before context compression | No |
| `Notification` | System notification | No |

**Configuration:** JSON in `.gemini/settings.json` at three levels: project, user (`~/.gemini/settings.json`), system (`/etc/gemini-cli/settings.json`).

**I/O:** JSON via stdin/stdout. Exit code 0 = success, 2 = block, other = warning.

**Environment Variables:** `GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR`, `GEMINI_SESSION_ID`, `GEMINI_CWD`, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` (compatibility alias).

**Management:** `/hooks panel`, `/hooks enable-all`, `/hooks disable-all`.

**Current Entire.io Integration Status (this project):** **NOT INSTALLED** — `.gemini/` directory exists (commands only) but no `settings.json` with Entire hooks.

_Source: [Google Developers Blog](https://developers.googleblog.com/tailor-gemini-cli-to-your-workflow-with-hooks/), [Gemini CLI Hooks Docs](https://geminicli.com/docs/hooks/)_

### OpenCode Plugin System

**30+ events, TypeScript/JavaScript plugin-based**

| Event Category | Key Events |
|---------------|------------|
| Session | `session.created`, `session.compacted`, `session.deleted`, `session.diff`, `session.error`, `session.idle`, `session.status`, `session.updated` |
| Tool | `tool.execute.before`, `tool.execute.after` |
| File | `file.edited`, `file.watcher.updated` |
| Message | `message.part.updated`, `message.part.removed`, `message.updated`, `message.removed` |
| Permission | `permission.asked`, `permission.replied` |
| Command | `command.executed` |
| TUI | `tui.prompt.append`, `tui.command.execute`, `tui.toast.show` |
| Experimental | `experimental.session.compacting` |

**Plugin Structure:**
```typescript
export const MyPlugin = async ({ project, client, $, directory, worktree }) => {
  return { /* hooks */ }
}
```

**Loading:** Place `.ts`/`.js` files in `.opencode/plugins/` (project) or `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` (global). npm plugins configured in `opencode.json` under `"plugin"` array; auto-installed via Bun.

**SDK:** Server-Sent Events (SSE) for programmatic control from external applications.

**Community:** Rich ecosystem including Oh My OpenCode (44 lifecycle hooks, 26+ tools, 11 specialized agents).

**Current Entire.io Integration Status (this project):** **NOT INSTALLED** — `.opencode/` directory exists (agents, commands, skills) but no `plugins/entire.ts`.

_Source: [OpenCode Plugins Docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/), [OpenCode Extensibility Guide](https://dev.to/einarcesar/does-opencode-support-hooks-a-complete-guide-to-extensibility-k3p)_

### Cross-Agent Hook Compatibility Matrix

| Capability | Claude Code | Gemini CLI | OpenCode |
|-----------|-------------|------------|----------|
| Hook Format | JSON (shell cmd) | JSON (shell cmd) | TypeScript plugin |
| Session Start/End | SessionStart/Stop | SessionStart/SessionEnd | session.created/session.idle |
| Tool Interception | PreToolUse/PostToolUse | BeforeTool/AfterTool | tool.execute.before/after |
| Context Compaction | PreCompact | PreCompress | experimental.session.compacting |
| Can Block Actions | PreToolUse only | BeforeAgent, BeforeTool, BeforeModel | tool.execute.before |
| Subagent Tracking | SubagentStop | N/A (AfterAgent covers) | N/A |
| Environment Vars | N/A | GEMINI_SESSION_ID, GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR | N/A (context object) |
| Stdin/Stdout Protocol | JSON | JSON | Function return |
| Config Location | `.claude/settings.json` | `.gemini/settings.json` | `.opencode/plugins/` |

_Confidence: HIGH — verified against official documentation for all three CLIs_

### Configuration Layering

All three CLIs and Entire.io use layered configuration with consistent precedence:

| Layer | Claude Code | Gemini CLI | OpenCode | Entire.io |
|-------|-------------|------------|----------|-----------|
| **Project** | `.claude/settings.json` | `.gemini/settings.json` | `.opencode/` | `.entire/settings.json` |
| **Personal** | `.claude/settings.local.json` | N/A | N/A | `.entire/settings.local.json` |
| **User/Global** | `~/.claude/settings.json` | `~/.gemini/settings.json` | `~/.config/opencode/` | `~/.config/entire/settings.json` |

_Source: [Entire Configuration](https://docs.entire.io/cli/configuration), respective CLI documentation_

### Technology Adoption Trends

**Agent-Agnostic Tooling:** Entire.io represents a growing trend of agent-agnostic developer tools. Rather than vendor lock-in to Anthropic/Google/OpenCode-specific solutions, Entire stores everything in Git — portable across agents.

**Hook Standardization:** All three CLIs now have hook/extension systems (Claude Code since late 2025, Gemini CLI hooks since v0.26.0 January 2026, OpenCode plugins since launch). The patterns are converging:
- Session lifecycle events
- Tool interception (before/after)
- Context compaction hooks
- Shell command execution model

**Community Ecosystem Growth:** Gemini CLI has 1M+ developers with an extension marketplace. OpenCode has Oh My OpenCode (44 hooks, 26+ tools). Claude Code has plugins and BMAD. This creates opportunities for cross-agent tooling.

**Known Limitations of Entire.io:**
- No retention policy for `entire/checkpoints/v1` (grows forever)
- Squash merges break bidirectional linking (trailers disappear)
- No PR linkage (branch names recorded but no PR number/URL)
- Full transcripts stored in pushable branches (privacy concern for public repos)
- Auto-summarization requires Claude CLI (not agent-agnostic for this feature)

_Source: [Under the Hood article](https://julien.danjou.info/blog/how-entire-works-under-the-hood/), [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues)_

## Integration Patterns Analysis

### Communication Protocols — Unified stdin/stdout JSON

All three CLIs use a conceptually similar hook communication pattern, but with important differences:

| Aspect | Claude Code | Gemini CLI | OpenCode |
|--------|-------------|------------|----------|
| **Transport** | stdin → stdout (JSON) | stdin → stdout (JSON) | Function call → return value |
| **Block signal** | Exit 2 OR `permissionDecision: "deny"` | Exit 2 OR `decision: "deny"` | `throw new Error()` |
| **Allow signal** | Exit 0 (empty stdout) | Exit 0 (empty stdout) | Return nothing |
| **Context injection** | `additionalContext` field in hookSpecificOutput | `systemMessage` or `additionalContext` | Modify args or return context |
| **Handler types** | Command, HTTP, Prompt, Agent | Command only | TypeScript/JavaScript function |
| **Timeout default** | 60s | 60s | N/A (sync JS execution) |
| **Async support** | Yes (background hooks with later injection) | No | Yes (async functions) |

**Key Insight for Entire.io:** The Entire.io CLI already implements adapter layers per agent. For Claude Code and Gemini CLI, it writes JSON shell command hooks into `settings.json`. For OpenCode, it generates a TypeScript plugin file at `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`. This means the protocol translation is handled by Entire.io — consumers don't need to care about per-CLI differences.

_Source: [Claude Code Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [Gemini CLI Hooks Reference](https://geminicli.com/docs/hooks/reference/), [OpenCode Plugins Docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/)_

### Hook Event Mapping Across CLIs

Entire.io needs to map its 7 lifecycle events to each CLI's event model:

| Entire.io Hook | Claude Code Event | Gemini CLI Event | OpenCode Event |
|----------------|-------------------|------------------|----------------|
| `SessionStart` | `SessionStart` | `SessionStart` | `session.created` |
| `SessionEnd` | `SessionEnd` | `SessionEnd` | `session.idle` or `session.deleted` |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | `UserPromptSubmit` | `BeforeAgent` | `tui.command.execute` |
| `Stop` (checkpoint trigger) | `Stop` | `AfterAgent` | `session.updated` |
| `PreToolUse` (subagent) | `PreToolUse` (matcher: `Agent`) | `BeforeTool` | `tool.execute.before` |
| `PostToolUse` (subagent) | `PostToolUse` (matcher: `Agent`) | `AfterTool` | `tool.execute.after` |
| `PostToolUse[TodoWrite]` | `PostToolUse` (matcher: `TodoWrite`) | `AfterTool` (matcher: `todo`) | `todo.updated` |

**Confidence: HIGH for Claude Code (GA), MEDIUM for Gemini/OpenCode (preview)**

_Source: [Under the Hood article](https://julien.danjou.info/blog/how-entire-works-under-the-hood/), respective CLI documentation_

### Context Injection Patterns — The Key Integration Point

The most valuable pattern for Cohezion's agent context awareness is **SessionStart context injection**. Each CLI supports injecting context when a session starts:

**Claude Code:**
```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "SessionStart",
    "additionalContext": "Context string injected into Claude's system prompt"
  }
}
```
The `additionalContext` is prepended to the first prompt. Non-JSON stdout from SessionStart hooks is also injected directly into context.

**Gemini CLI:**
```json
{
  "systemMessage": "Context injected as system message",
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "additionalContext": "Additional context appended to prompt"
  }
}
```
Both `systemMessage` and `additionalContext` are supported. The `source` field in input (`startup|resume|clear`) allows different injection behavior per trigger.

**OpenCode:**
```typescript
export const ContextPlugin = async ({ project }) => ({
  hooks: {
    "session.created": async (input) => {
      // Inject context via custom tool or tui.prompt.append
    },
    "experimental.session.compacting": async (input) => {
      // Inject context that survives compaction
    }
  }
})
```
OpenCode uses `experimental.session.compacting` for context that must survive compaction — critical for persistent session awareness.

_Source: [Claude Code Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [Gemini CLI Hooks Reference](https://geminicli.com/docs/hooks/reference/), [OpenCode Plugins](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/)_

### Entire.io Data Access Patterns

For context injection to work, a SessionStart hook needs to query Entire.io's data. Available CLI commands:

| Command | Output | Use Case |
|---------|--------|----------|
| `entire status` | Active sessions, agent types, token counts | "What's happening now across all agents?" |
| `entire explain --short` | Checkpoint list with session summaries | "What was accomplished in recent sessions?" |
| `entire explain --checkpoint <id> --short` | Single checkpoint summary | "What did session X do?" |
| `entire explain --session <id>` | All checkpoints for a session | "Full history of a specific session" |
| `entire explain --generate` | AI-generated summary (requires Claude CLI) | "Summarize what happened for injection" |

**Performance Characteristics:**
- `entire status`: ~200ms (reads local metadata)
- `entire explain --short`: ~500ms (reads checkpoint branch)
- `entire explain --generate`: 3-10s (calls Claude CLI for AI summary)
- `entire rewind --list`: ~300ms (reads shadow branches)

**Integration Pattern: SessionStart → entire status → format → inject as context**

A shell hook can be shared across Claude Code and Gemini CLI (both use shell commands). OpenCode requires a TypeScript wrapper that shells out to the `entire` binary.

_Source: [Entire CLI Commands](https://docs.entire.io/cli/commands), local testing on this project_

### Cross-Agent Session Visibility Architecture

The core architectural challenge: making each agent aware of what other agents are doing in parallel. The data flow:

```
Agent A (Claude Code) starts session
  └→ Entire hooks capture SessionStart
      └→ Shadow branch created
          └→ Checkpoints accumulate on turns

Agent B (Gemini CLI) starts session
  └→ SessionStart hook fires
      └→ Hook runs: entire status
          └→ Sees Agent A's active session
              └→ Injects: "Claude Code session active on branch X, working on Y"
```

**Conflict Detection Pattern:**
```
SessionStart hook:
  1. Run `entire status` → parse JSON output
  2. Filter for sessions on same branch or touching same files
  3. If overlap detected → inject warning context
  4. If no overlap → inject awareness context (FYI only)
```

**File-Level Conflict Detection (Advanced):**
```
Stop/AfterAgent hook:
  1. Run `entire explain --checkpoint <latest> --short`
  2. Extract files_touched list
  3. Compare against other active sessions' files_touched
  4. If overlap → inject merge-risk warning
```

_Source: Architecture derived from [Entire.io Core Concepts](https://docs.entire.io/core-concepts) and [Under the Hood](https://julien.danjou.info/blog/how-entire-works-under-the-hood/)_

### Security Patterns

**Secret Redaction:** Entire.io performs best-effort redaction of API keys, tokens, and credentials when writing to `entire/checkpoints/v1`. However:
- Shadow branches during active sessions may contain unredacted data
- Redaction is pattern-based, not comprehensive
- Public repos expose full session transcripts

**Hook Security:**
- Claude Code: Hooks run with user permissions, outside the Bash tool sandbox
- Gemini CLI: Project-level hooks fingerprinted; warns on changes from git pull
- OpenCode: Plugin hooks don't intercept subagent tool calls (known bug — [Issue #5894](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/5894))

**Recommendation for Cohezion:** Since Cohezion is a private repo with sensitive research data:
1. Use `.entire/settings.local.json` for any API keys in summarization config
2. Review `entire/checkpoints/v1` before pushing to remote
3. Consider `--skip-push-sessions` for sensitive branches

## Architectural Patterns and Design

### Recommended System Architecture: Observer-Mediated Hub-and-Spoke

After analyzing multi-agent coordination patterns, the architecture that best fits Cohezion's Entire.io integration is a **hub-and-spoke pattern with observer-mediated context sharing**, where Entire.io serves as the hub and each agent CLI is a spoke.

```
                    ┌──────────────────────┐
                    │   Entire.io Hub      │
                    │  (Git Shadow Branch)  │
                    │  entire/checkpoints   │
                    │  /v1 metadata         │
                    └──────┬───────────────┘
                           │
              ┌────────────┼────────────────┐
              │            │                │
    ┌─────────▼──┐  ┌─────▼──────┐  ┌──────▼─────┐
    │ Claude Code │  │ Gemini CLI │  │  OpenCode  │
    │   Hooks     │  │   Hooks    │  │  Plugin    │
    │ (JSON cmd)  │  │ (JSON cmd) │  │ (TS func)  │
    └─────────────┘  └────────────┘  └────────────┘
```

**Why this pattern over alternatives:**

| Pattern | Fit | Reason |
|---------|-----|--------|
| Hub-and-Spoke (Entire.io as hub) | **Best** | Entire.io already acts as centralized session store; agents don't need to talk directly to each other |
| Peer-to-Peer (agents talk directly) | Poor | No agent-to-agent protocol exists; CLIs don't know about each other |
| Blackboard (shared memory space) | Medium | Git shadow branches are a blackboard, but too slow for real-time coordination |
| Orchestrator-Worker | Poor | No single agent coordinates others; all agents are independent |

**Key architectural insight:** We don't need agents to communicate with each other in real-time. We need each agent to be **aware of what other agents have done and are doing** when it starts. This is a read-only context injection problem, not a bidirectional communication problem. Entire.io's existing `entire status` command provides the data; we just need hooks to inject it.

_Source: [Google's Multi-Agent Patterns (InfoQ)](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/01/multi-agent-design-patterns/), [Microsoft Multi-Agent Reference Architecture](https://microsoft.github.io/multi-agent-reference-architecture/docs/reference-architecture/Patterns.html), [Event-Driven Multi-Agent Systems (Confluent)](https://www.confluent.io/blog/event-driven-multi-agent-systems/)_

### Cross-Runtime Translation Pattern (Lessons from GSD)

The [GSD project](https://github.com/gsd-build/get-shit-done) (used at Amazon, Google, Shopify, Webflow) solved the exact same cross-runtime problem: one codebase targeting Claude Code, OpenCode, and Gemini CLI. Their architecture provides a proven pattern:

**Canonical Format + Install-Time Transformation:**
```
Canonical (Claude Code format)
    ↓
[Runtime Detector]
    ├→ Claude Code: Copy unchanged to ~/.claude/
    ├→ OpenCode: Flatten commands, map tools, convert frontmatter → ~/.config/opencode/
    └→ Gemini CLI: Convert MD→TOML, normalize tools, strip MCP → ~/.gemini/
```

**Key Transformations Required:**

| Aspect | Claude Code | Gemini CLI | OpenCode |
|--------|-------------|------------|----------|
| Hook format | JSON in `settings.json` | JSON in `settings.json` | TypeScript in `plugins/` |
| Tool names | PascalCase (`Read`, `Write`) | snake_case (`read_file`, `write_file`) | lowercase (`read`, `write`) |
| Command structure | Nested dirs | TOML files | Flat files |
| Config location | `~/.claude/` | `~/.gemini/` | `~/.config/opencode/` |

**Relevance to Cohezion:** Entire.io already implements per-agent adapters (JSON for Claude/Gemini, TypeScript for OpenCode). Our custom context injection hooks should follow the same pattern — write the logic once in a shell script, then wrap it for each runtime.

_Source: [GSD Architecture (DeepWiki)](https://deepwiki.com/gsd-build/get-shit-done), [One Codebase Three Runtimes (Rick Hightower)](https://medium.com/@richardhightower/one-codebase-three-runtimes-how-gsd-targets-claude-code-opencode-and-gemini-cli-29c98cfe96c6)_

### Context Injection Architecture

The core architectural component is a **SessionStart context injector** — a hook/plugin that runs when any agent starts a session and injects awareness of parallel sessions.

**Proposed Architecture:**

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ SessionStart Hook (shared shell script)              │
│                                                      │
│  1. entire status --quiet → parse active sessions    │
│  2. Filter: same branch? same files? conflicts?      │
│  3. Format: concise context string                   │
│  4. Return: JSON with additionalContext               │
└──────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                   │
     ┌─────────────┼─────────────────────┐
     │             │                     │
┌────▼────┐  ┌────▼────┐  ┌─────────────▼──────────┐
│ Claude  │  │ Gemini  │  │ OpenCode               │
│ Hook    │  │ Hook    │  │ Plugin                  │
│ wrapper │  │ wrapper │  │ wrapper                 │
│ (JSON)  │  │ (JSON)  │  │ (TS → shell out)       │
└─────────┘  └─────────┘  └────────────────────────┘
```

**Three-layer design:**

1. **Core Logic Layer** (`entire-context.sh`): A single shell script that queries `entire status`, formats context, and outputs JSON. Agent-agnostic — pure data transformation.

2. **Adapter Layer** (per-CLI wrappers):
   - Claude Code: Shell hook in `.claude/settings.json` that calls `entire-context.sh` and returns `{ hookSpecificOutput: { additionalContext: "..." } }`
   - Gemini CLI: Shell hook in `.gemini/settings.json` that calls `entire-context.sh` and returns `{ systemMessage: "..." }`
   - OpenCode: TypeScript plugin in `.opencode/plugins/entire-context.ts` that shells out to `entire-context.sh` and returns context via the plugin API

3. **Output Format Layer**: Each adapter formats the core logic output into the CLI-specific JSON/return format.

**Design Principles:**
- **DRY:** Core logic written once, adapters are thin wrappers
- **Fail-open:** If `entire status` fails, the hook returns empty context (no blocking)
- **Performance budget:** <500ms total (entire status ~200ms + formatting ~50ms + overhead ~250ms)
- **Non-blocking:** If hook exceeds timeout, agent starts without context (graceful degradation)

_Source: Architecture derived from [Claude Code Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [Gemini CLI Hooks](https://geminicli.com/docs/hooks/), [OpenCode Plugins](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/), and GSD translation pattern_

### Data Architecture: Entire.io's Git-Native Storage

Entire.io's storage architecture uses Git primitives exclusively — no external databases, no cloud services, no additional infrastructure:

```
Git Repository
├── main (your code, clean history)
├── entire/<hash>-<worktree-id> (temporary shadow branches, local only)
└── entire/checkpoints/v1 (permanent metadata, pushable)
    └── a3/b2c4d5e6f7/
        ├── metadata.json    # summary, attribution, tokens
        ├── 0/
        │   ├── full.jsonl   # complete transcript
        │   ├── prompt.txt   # user prompts
        │   └── context.md   # context snapshot
        └── 1/               # additional sessions
```

**Architectural Strengths:**
- Zero infrastructure cost (uses Git you already have)
- Collision-free multi-developer pushes (12-char random hex IDs)
- Tree union merges (no merge conflicts on `entire/checkpoints/v1`)
- Content-addressable deduplication (identical files share blobs)
- Transport for free (git push/pull handles distribution)

**Architectural Weaknesses:**
- No retention policy (metadata branch grows forever)
- Squash merges destroy commit trailers (breaks bidirectional links)
- No real-time session visibility (must query CLI for status)
- Transcript privacy concerns for public repos
- No query indexing (linear scan for searches)

_Source: [How Entire Works Under the Hood](https://julien.danjou.info/blog/how-entire-works-under-the-hood/), [Entire Core Concepts](https://docs.entire.io/core-concepts)_

### Scalability and Performance Considerations

| Concern | Current State | Mitigation |
|---------|---------------|------------|
| Shadow branch accumulation | `entire clean` for local cleanup | Schedule periodic cleanup via cron or git hook |
| Checkpoint metadata growth | No retention policy | Implement custom `entire/checkpoints/v1` pruning script |
| SessionStart hook latency | ~200-500ms for `entire status` | Cache status output for 30s; invalidate on git commit |
| Transcript size per session | Can exceed 1MB per session | Not a concern for context injection (we only read metadata, not transcripts) |
| Multiple concurrent sessions | 24 active sessions on this project | `entire status` handles this; output grows linearly with sessions |
| Git checkout heaviness | Thousands of turns accumulate data | `entire/checkpoints/v1` is metadata-only (JSON, not code) |

**Performance Budget for Context Injection:**
```
SessionStart hook total budget: 1000ms (well within 60s timeout)
  ├── entire status:     ~200ms
  ├── JSON parsing:      ~50ms
  ├── Formatting:        ~50ms
  ├── Adapter overhead:  ~100ms
  └── Margin:            ~600ms
```

_Source: Local performance measurements, [Entire Configuration](https://docs.entire.io/cli/configuration)_

### Security Architecture

**Threat Model for Cross-Agent Context Injection:**

| Threat | Risk | Mitigation |
|--------|------|------------|
| Sensitive data in injected context | Medium | Context injection uses `entire status` (session metadata only, not transcripts) |
| Hook tampering via git pull | Medium | Gemini CLI fingerprints project hooks; warns on changes. Claude Code requires explicit approval. OpenCode uses trusted plugin dirs. |
| Secret leakage in checkpoints | High for public repos | Entire performs best-effort redaction; recommend `--skip-push-sessions` for sensitive branches |
| Subagent bypass of hooks | Known bug (OpenCode) | OpenCode `tool.execute.before` doesn't intercept subagent calls ([Issue #5894](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/5894)) |
| Stale session data injection | Low | Status is live (not cached); stale data is misleading but not harmful |

**Recommended Security Posture:**
1. Context injection hooks should ONLY query `entire status` (metadata) — never raw transcripts
2. Use `.entire/settings.local.json` for any API keys (gitignored)
3. Review `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch before pushing to public remotes
4. For Cohezion (private repo): moderate risk; standard precautions sufficient

_Source: [Entire Configuration](https://docs.entire.io/cli/configuration), [GitHub README Security Section](https://github.com/entireio/cli)_

The complete traceability chain connecting BMAD planning artifacts to Entire.io session data:

BMAD PRD (FR-X.Y)

          └→ Story (Story 12.X)

### Phase 2: Context Injection Hook — Core Logic (Effort: ~2-4 hours)

Build the shared shell script that queries Entire.io and formats context for injection.

**File: `.claude/hooks/entire-context.sh`**

Design requirements:
- Query `entire status` for active sessions
- Format output as concise context string (budget: <500 tokens)
- Output valid JSON with `additionalContext` field
- Fail gracefully (return empty context on any error)
- Execute in <500ms

**Context Format Design:**
```
🔄 Entire.io Active Sessions (3 total):
- Claude Code [e9757f9] on branch security/hardening — working on "Entire.io integration research" (1h ago, 1.6M tokens)
- Claude Code [9da42dd] on branch main — working on "Obsidian vault research" (10m ago)
- Gemini CLI [abc1234] on branch feature/auth — working on "OAuth implementation" (5m ago)

⚠️ Potential conflict: Sessions e9757f9 and abc1234 both touch src/cohezion/api/
```

**Testing approach:**
```bash

```

_Source: [Claude Code Hooks Testing](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [Gemini CLI Writing Hooks](https://geminicli.com/docs/hooks/writing-hooks/)_

### Phase 3: Per-CLI Adapters (Effort: ~2-3 hours)

**Claude Code Adapter** — Thin wrapper, JSON output:

Register in `.claude/settings.json` under `SessionStart`:
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": ".claude/hooks/entire-context.sh",
            "timeout": 5000
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Gemini CLI Adapter** — Same shell script, register in `.gemini/settings.json`:
```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionStart": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          {
            "name": "entire-context",
            "type": "command",
            "command": ".claude/hooks/entire-context.sh",
            "timeout": 5000
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

**OpenCode Adapter** — TypeScript wrapper that shells out:

File: `.opencode/plugins/entire-context.ts`
```typescript
export const EntireContextPlugin = async ({ $ }) => ({
  hooks: {
    "session.created": async () => {
      try {
        const result = await $`bash .claude/hooks/entire-context.sh`.quiet()
        // Parse and use context from stdout
      } catch {
        // Fail gracefully - no context injection
      }
    }
  }
})
```

**Key constraint for Gemini CLI:** "Your script must not print any plain text to stdout other than the final JSON object." The core script must be disciplined about stdout — all debug output to stderr.

_Source: [Gemini CLI Hooks Best Practices](https://geminicli.com/docs/hooks/best-practices/), [OpenCode Plugins](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/), [Claude Code Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)_

### Phase 4: Conflict Detection (Effort: ~3-4 hours)

Add file-level overlap detection to the Stop/AfterAgent hooks.

**Logic:**
1. When an agent finishes a turn (Stop event), extract modified files from the current session
2. Query `entire status` for other active sessions
3. Cross-reference file lists for overlap
4. If overlap detected, inject a warning into the next turn's context

**Implementation approach:**
- Use `entire explain --checkpoint <latest> --short` to extract files touched
- Parse against `entire status` output for other sessions' file lists
- Write a separate `entire-conflict-check.sh` script registered on the `Stop`/`AfterAgent` event

**Confidence: MEDIUM** — This requires parsing Entire.io's explain output for file lists, which may not be fully structured JSON. May need to fall back to `git diff` within shadow branches.

### Phase 5: Traceability Integration (Effort: ~4-6 hours)

Connect the Entire.io checkpoint chain to BMAD planning artifacts.

**Squash Merge Workaround:**

Since `cz worktree sync` uses squash merge (destroying trailers), we need to preserve checkpoint references:

Option A — **Checkpoint metadata in squash commit body:**
```bash
# Before squash, extract checkpoint IDs from feature branch
git log --format='%b' feature-branch | grep 'Entire-Checkpoint:' > /tmp/checkpoints
# Include in squash commit message body
```

Option B — **External mapping file:**
Store a `checkpoint-story-map.json` in the vault that maps checkpoint IDs to story IDs:
```json
{
  "a3b2c4d5e6f7": { "story": "12.1", "epic": "12", "branch": "session-42-feature" },
  "f7e6d5c4b3a2": { "story": "12.2", "epic": "12", "branch": "session-43-auth" }
}
```

Option C — **Post-sync hook** that records the mapping in vault/SurrealDB before the worktree is cleaned up.

**Recommended: Option C** — Most automated, least error-prone, integrates with existing Cohezion vault infrastructure.

**Hook Development Cycle:**

# 6. Test in Gemini CLI

# 7. Test in OpenCode

```

**Debugging tools:**
- Claude Code: `claude --debug` for hook execution details, `/hooks` to verify config
- Gemini CLI: stderr for all debug output, `/hooks panel` for status
- OpenCode: `client.app.log()` for structured logging
- All: `echo '{"test":"data"}' | ./hook.sh` for standalone testing

_Source: [Claude Code Hooks Reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), [Gemini CLI Writing Hooks](https://geminicli.com/docs/hooks/writing-hooks/), [DataCamp Hooks Guide](https://www.datacamp.com/tutorial/claude-code-hooks)_

### Team Organization and Skills

**No new skills required.** The implementation uses:
- Shell scripting (bash) — core hook logic
- JSON parsing (`jq`) — stdin/stdout protocol
- TypeScript — OpenCode plugin wrapper only
- Git — understanding shadow branches and checkpoint metadata

**All implementation can be done by a single developer** working across sessions. No external team coordination needed. The hooks are local developer tooling with zero CI/CD impact.

### Cost Optimization

| Component | Cost | Notes |
|-----------|------|-------|
| Entire.io CLI | **Free** | Open source, MIT license |
| Hook scripts | **Free** | Local shell scripts |
| Shadow branches | **~0 bytes** (deduplicated) | Git content-addressable storage |
| Checkpoint metadata | **~1-5KB per checkpoint** | JSON metadata only |
| Auto-summarization | **~$0.001-0.01 per summary** | Uses Claude CLI for AI summary (optional) |
| Total monthly cost | **~$0** | Unless auto-summarization is enabled at high frequency |

### Risk Assessment and Mitigation

| Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|-------------|--------|------------|
| Entire.io Gemini/OpenCode preview breaks | Medium | Low | `entire enable --force` to reinstall; hooks are independent per agent |
| Hook timeout blocks agent startup | Low | High | Set `timeout: 5000` (5s); fail-open design returns empty context |
| `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch bloat | Medium | Medium | Periodic `entire clean`; custom retention script |
| Squash merge breaks traceability | High (by design) | Medium | Post-sync hook records mapping before cleanup (Phase 5, Option C) |
| Secret leakage in checkpoints | Low (private repo) | High | `--skip-push-sessions` for sensitive branches; review before push |
| 15 stuck sessions cause issues | High (exists now) | Low | `entire doctor --force` to clean up immediately |
| Hook conflicts with existing Entire hooks | Low | Medium | Register custom hooks as separate entries in the same event arrays |
| OpenCode subagent bypass | Known bug | Medium | Accept risk; monitor [Issue #5894](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/5894) for fix |

| JSON parsing | jq | python3 -c | jq is faster for simple extraction; python3 as fallback |

Here's what I found about **Entire.io** and its latest updates:

## Entire.io — Overview

Entire.io is building a developer platform where agents and humans can collaborate, interact, and grow. They describe the launch as "the birth of a new galaxy in this universe."

## What Entire.io Does

Entire is a new developer platform that hooks into your Git workflow to capture AI agent sessions on every push, unifying your code with its context and reasoning. It introduces **Checkpoints**, a new primitive that automatically captures agent context as first-class, versioned data in Git.

## Founder & Vision

Built by former GitHub CEO Thomas Dohmke, Entire.io is not here to replace Git. Instead, it acts as a "semantic reasoning layer" to capture the context behind AI-generated code.

## How It Works — Agent Integration

- Entire.io does not replace Git. Your code still lives in Git. Instead, Entire acts as a middle layer. It sits between the AI agent and your Git repository, recording the "thought process" of the AI while Git records the final files.

- **Sessions & Checkpoints:** Sessions are stored separately from your code commits on the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. A checkpoint is a snapshot within a session that you can rewind to — a "save point" in your work. Checkpoints are created when you or the agent make a git commit.

- **Shadow Branches:** Entire solves the problem of large AI logs using Shadow Branches. Instead of stuffing all AI context into your main codebase, Entire creates an invisible, parallel timeline (called `entire/checkpoints/v1`). Your main branch stays perfectly clean and fast. The shadow branch holds all the heavy AI logs.

## Key Feature: Rewind

Entire.io acts like a DVR for your code. Because it creates a Checkpoint after every single AI thought, you can just type `entire rewind`. This instantly rewinds your project back to the exact minute before the AI messed up. You keep your good progress and only erase the AI's mistakes.

## Why It Matters

Git was built for humans typing on keyboards. It was never built for AI agents like Claude Code or Google Gemini generating massive chunks of code in seconds. Git is incredible at tracking the final result, but it completely ignores the journey.

---

**Note:** As of the latest search results, Entire.io has not published a detailed March 2026 roadmap or a specific feature update for this month. The platform appears to still be in its early/launch phase with its CLI tool available on GitHub. The core value proposition centers on bridging the gap between traditional Git workflows and modern AI agent-driven development through checkpoints, session tracking, and rewind capabilities.

input.new_string:
This research investigates how to build automated cross-agent context awareness using [Entire.io](https://github.com/entireio/cli) (v0.4.9) across three AI coding CLIs: Claude Code, Gemini CLI (v0.32.0), and OpenCode (v1.2.16). The Cohezion project currently runs up to 24 parallel agent sessions, but each starts cold with no awareness of what other sessions are doing — leading to duplicated work and file-level conflicts.

The research covers Entire.io's Git-native architecture (shadow branches, checkpoint metadata on orphan `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch, JSONL transcript parsing), the hook/extension systems of all three CLIs (12 lifecycle events in Claude Code, 11 in Gemini CLI, 30+ in OpenCode), integration patterns for cross-agent session visibility, and a concrete 5-phase implementation roadmap. All technical claims are verified against official documentation and community sources from early 2026.

**Critical finding:** Entire.io hooks are only installed for Claude Code on this project.
